title: Ethics You Can Actually Use
intro: Talking about ethics isn't a practice. Calabro borrows psychology's APA Ethics Code — adopted in 1953 when that field moved from academia into practice, much like UX today.

learn.title: Five principles, applied
learn.text:
**Respect for rights and dignity** — informed consent, the right to withdraw, privacy and confidentiality.
**Competence** — only take on work you're qualified to do; get help when you aren't.
**Integrity** — honest reporting: no overclaiming, no cherry-picking.
**Professional responsibility** — methods that fit the question; accountability for findings.
**Concern for welfare** — avoid harm and distress; protect vulnerable participants.

Calabro adds **social responsibility**: consider the wider effects of what the research enables.

try.q: Which principle covers “no cherry-picking the quotes that support the roadmap”?

learn.title: Consent in practice
learn.text:
Consent must be **understandable, voluntary and revocable** — not a wall of legal text.

Store and share recordings and data to a security standard, and only for as long as they are needed.

Remove rare details that could identify someone, even when the name has been taken off.

try.q: A transcript has no name but mentions a very unusual job title at a named company. What should you do?
options: Keep it — the name is already gone
Ask the participant to approve the quote
Store it in a restricted folder
try.explain: Rare details can identify someone on their own.

left.label: Consent theatre
items: Names removed, rare details left in

right.label: Real consent
items: Kept only as long as needed

learn.title: The research you shouldn't run
learn.text:
Don't run research whose only purpose is to make a decided product look validated.

That is both an integrity problem and a professional-responsibility one: the method doesn't fit the question, because there is no real question.

try.q: A team has decided to ship and asks for a study to prove users like it. Which principles are at stake?
try.explain: Honest reporting, and methods that fit a real question.
